brief: extend the verdict JSON shape with build.depends_on + the existing commit stamp; build tools/verdict-staleness.mjs to report fresh/stale/unknown; back-fill depends_on honestly for existing wave-1 verdicts; --self-test that goes red both ways; wire into tools/publish.mjs as a reported number, not a gate
outputs_written: tools/publish.mjs (staleness summary printed after the score-plot check, never sets process.exitCode)
tools/progress.mjs (docs/progress.html stat card + a 'Verdict staleness' table, same reported-not-gated posture)
findings: Ran for real against the 33 verdict files under corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/: 1 fresh, 28 stale, 4 unknown at the commit this task finished on. The unknown count matters more than the headline ratio because it names the ceiling of what this tool can currently see — 2 of the 4 unknowns are a build.commit_sha that no longer resolves in this repository's history (rewritten/short refs from early wave-1 verdicts), the other 2 are a missing commit_sha entirely; none is 'no depends_on' any more, because the backfill left nothing absent this round (every verdict named at least one resolvable probe script).

depends_on was derived ONLY from structured fields — build.harness_commands[].command, artifacts[].produced_by, artifacts[].path — never from free prose (checks[].detail, why_not_ten, critic.instrument_independence). That distinction is load-bearing: W1-15-r2's own instrument_independence text names tools/harness/w1-15-coupling.mjs specifically to say it was NEVER run; a naive text scan over the whole verdict would have recorded a dependency on a file the verdict explicitly disclaims using.

Two shared libraries have a documented whole-tree contract rather than a narrow import list, and the backfill honours that rather than under-counting it: tools/lib/browser.mjs boots the real page, and game/src/engine.js statically imports essentially the entire engine and fetches game/data/index.json at boot — so any probe that drives the browser genuinely depends on the whole of game/src/** and game/data/**, not just the one import line. tools/lib/gamedata.mjs and tools/lib/combat-node.mjs get the same treatment per their own header comments.

--self-test does not fabricate a commit (this task must not commit, and a synthetic commit could not exercise the real git plumbing anyway). It finds the most recent REAL commit that touched game/src/, takes its parent as the fixture, and checks both directions against the real diff to HEAD. Verified it actually goes red: patched matchesAny() to always return true, then always return false, ran --self-test each time, watched the expected case fail each time (not the same case both times — proving the two directions are independently checked), then restored and re-verified 6/6.

Wired into tools/publish.mjs and tools/progress.mjs as a reported number only — computeReport() is wrapped in try/catch in both call sites and NEVER sets process.exitCode or blocks the page. Argued explicitly in tools/verdict-staleness.mjs's own header against the tools/check-quests.mjs precedent: a shared gate that fails everyone's publish over one piece's already-stale commit is the exact four-times-paid failure check-quests.mjs's header documents fixing, reintroduced one level up.

docs/progress.html now carries a 'Verdicts fresh at HEAD' stat card and a full 'Verdict staleness' table (piece, status, commit, reason) — this satisfies the brief's 'the progress page should say how many verdicts are still standing on current code' literally, not just as a publish-time console line.
next_step: none — done. A natural follow-up for a later piece: as new verdicts are filed, RI-MTH04's evidence-block convention (or a critic checklist) could require build.depends_on at write time rather than relying on a later backfill pass; verdict-validate.mjs could then WARN (not error, per its own convention for pre-existing verdicts) when depends_on is absent on a NEW verdict.
notes_for_successor: Do not turn verdict-staleness into a gate anywhere — see the header of tools/verdict-staleness.mjs for the argued reason, which mirrors tools/check-quests.mjs's own history. If a verdict looks stale, the correct action is to tell whoever owns the next round, not to touch the verdict's score or delete it — RULES.md is explicit that staleness is information, not a downgrade.
